chapter: Brother Remus and the brass bands
title: Remus and Bebe in brass bands and the Imperial and Superior orchestras
summary: Remus on bass drum in Allen's band, Bebe in dance bands, and how bands were named.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: That's our dance. I wondered about Ramus, your oldest brother. Which brass band did he work with?

Allen was his famous band. That was the main one. Allen, the old man Henry Allen brass band. Mm-hmm. Was his favorite band. And he played bass drummers there. He was strictly the bass drum player in that band because...

Allen's brother was a snare drum player, George Allen. He lived over there, but he went back home and died in Morgan City. He got two old cities. Did he play in any of the other bands? Yeah, he played extra with the other bands. Like I tell you, he played extra with me. When I was, they tell me to get the Trummel House in Barnes, they tell me, I said, well they had to do this right across the street for me. He said, Bill, you play Trummel today, get your brother on a drum. I said, okay, we have a funeral like that, I said, I can't get off. I said, huh? I'll get a dream or something. They had three, four, five funerals a week like that. I said, Allison, sometimes he play with his orchestra, you know. I said, you play with the brass band, because I was waking every night out in Lake David, Piron Ambulance. He said, you play Trummel and use your brother on snare drum. He said, okay. I said, okay, we'll tell him.
Did he ever play any dance bands much? Remus?
My brother, Remus? Yes. Never had. Never did play. No more than at the fairground. Then they have two bands, had brass band at the fairground and, you know, orchestra and the side and stuff.
And you mentioned Bebe played with Lindsey and then he played with Manuel Perez. Was there any other bands that you remember?
Other bands too. He was one of the first, I mean one of the hit snare drum players in the Humboldt band, my brother's been big. Yeah.
Did he ever play with any of the other dance bands like Celestan or the Superior or any of

Bay Bay. That was his band, the Superior band, orchestra. He played in that band. Oh, it's pitching in the paper. He used to play with all the old gasp and them, and I'm going to raise them, that's what I tell you. I used to help him carry the drums and play with them. Was that Imperial or Superior? Imperial. Imperial.

Imperial. Yeah, the Imperial and Superior. They see bands, them days they didn't go by a man's name. They didn't go by a man's name, they didn't go by a man's name, they didn't go by a man's name like you go by a certain person, they didn't go that way, they go taking the name. Now when me and Sammy Morgan was playing together, Sammy Morgan was playing with the Magnolia band. Yeah. You understand, the Magnolia band, Sammy Morgan was playing trumpet. But one had a band, Buddy Petit and John Robichaud, they didn't even by their band. But Buddy Petit had his own band like that, you know, his name. And from that they all started to sing like that. And Risley, he made up his band out of Jack Sheen. And they call it the, you know, Risley's band.
